findings.premise: Every epic-level non-goal in the approved DEF (no daemon/indexer dependency added to the reusable package; no multimodal/cross-user sync/profiling) is honored by the HLD's architecture and is not silently built.
findings.evidence: DEF.md §3 Non-goals: 'Add daemon/indexer dependencies to the reusable package. — Independent external applications must consume the feature without insrc startup.' HLD §3 mirrors this exactly: 'Do not import src/daemon, src/config, src/db connection singletons or global insrc PATHS from this package.' No multimodal/cross-user-sync capability appears anywhere in the HLD's contracts or stories. [files: docs/epics/share-project-memory-across-agents-applications-E2026110117123b6d/DEF.md, docs/epics/share-project-memory-across-agents-applications-E2026110117123b6d/HLD.md]

findings.premise: Every DEF story (S001–S009) has exactly one owning HLD shared contract and one HLD story-boundary section, with no DEF story left undesigned and no HLD story invented beyond the DEF.
findings.evidence: DEF.md §6 lists stories S001–S009 (lines 94–213). HLD §5/§6 define sc1↔s1 through sc10↔s9 and story-boundary sections 6.1–6.9 for the identical nine story IDs in the identical dependency order (s1→s9 depends-on chain matches DEF's per-story 'Depends on' lines). [files: docs/epics/share-project-memory-across-agents-applications-E2026110117123b6d/DEF.md, docs/epics/share-project-memory-across-agents-applications-E2026110117123b6d/HLD.md]

findings.premise: The HLD's claim that 'no reusable global model-concurrency scheduler is established by the current grounding' and that 'insrc per-role routing selects models; its serial-await convention is not a runtime mutex' is true of the code today.
findings.evidence: src/daemon/queue.ts implements a two-lane job scheduler ('index' and 'summary') that is specific to IndexJob objects for the code-index/document-summary pipeline — it yields the summary lane to the index lane (Story 0f0e4f45) but exposes no generic cross-caller model-concurrency primitive a new, unrelated package could depend on. No other module-local or global dispatcher for arbitrary ModelPort calls exists. [files: src/daemon/queue.ts]

findings.premise: The HLD's implicit claim that LanceDB access today is a single shared connection singleton scoped to PATHS.lance and owned exclusively by the daemon (not a 'dedicated connection per directory' already available for reuse) is true, so the new package's per-directory connection is a genuinely new mechanism rather than a reuse of existing plumbing.
findings.evidence: src/db/lance/conn.ts: getLanceConn() is a lazy-init module-level singleton (`_instance`), and LanceStoreNotOwnerError fires only when `resolveStorePath(_path) === resolveStorePath(PATHS.lance)` — i.e. ownership enforcement and the singleton are both hard-wired to the one index-store path, not parameterized per directory. [files: src/db/lance/conn.ts]

findings.premise: packages/project-memory, named throughout §3 as the new package, does not already exist in the repository.
findings.evidence: Glob for packages/project-memory/** and packages/** both returned no files — no packages/ directory exists in this repo at all.

findings.premise: The 'independently built ESM package with its own package.json/tsconfig living as a sibling directory inside this monorepo' pattern the HLD proposes to reuse is an already-established precedent, not a hypothetical shape.
findings.evidence: vscode-plugin/package.json and jetbrains-plugin/build.gradle.kts both exist today as independently built sibling packages inside this same repository, confirming the sibling-package pattern the HLD leans on for packages/project-memory is real and already proven here. [files: vscode-plugin/package.json, jetbrains-plugin/build.gradle.kts]

findings.premise: The ten shared-contract interface sketches (sc1–sc10) cross-reference each other's types consistently — no contract consumes a type that a different contract does not actually define.
findings.evidence: sc2 defines Scope, MemoryCommand, OperationReceipt, ReadRequest, SearchRequest, InspectRequest; sc3's QueueFrame.command: MemoryCommand, sc4's CommitPlan.scope: Scope, and sc6's RecallService.context(request: ReadRequest)/search(request: SearchRequest)/inspect(request: InspectRequest) all resolve directly against sc2's definitions with matching field names, with no orphaned or redefined type found across sc1–sc10. [files: docs/epics/share-project-memory-across-agents-applications-E2026110117123b6d/HLD.md]

findings.premise: The HLD's proposed change site (a new packages/project-memory with 'independent build/test consumption') has a concrete path into this repo's existing build tooling (root package.json has no workspaces mechanism today), so the inventory of change sites for s1 is complete.
findings.evidence: Root package.json (name @insrc/backend) declares no "workspaces" field and no monorepo build tool; its only build script is 'tsc --inlineSources && ... && node copy-assets.mjs' over the existing src/ tree. The HLD states all packages/project-memory paths are 'proposed, not existing code' and defers lock-primitive/cross-platform qualification to s1, but never names how the new package's independent build/test loop will be wired into (or deliberately kept outside of) this root build — I could not confirm from the HLD text or current repo config whether that integration point is an open decision s1 must resolve or an oversight. [files: package.json, docs/epics/share-project-memory-across-agents-applications-E2026110117123b6d/HLD.md]
findings.action: Confirm in s1's LLD whether packages/project-memory is built via a new npm workspace, a fully separate toolchain, or publish-and-consume, and record that choice explicitly rather than leaving it implicit.

findings.premise: The new package's dedicated per-directory LanceDB connection does not redesign or collide with the existing index-store Lance connection's ownership guard, which an earlier epic (c2ba6fa6) already established.
findings.evidence: src/db/lance/conn.ts's LanceStoreNotOwnerError check is scoped strictly to `resolveStorePath(_path) === resolveStorePath(PATHS.lance)`; a distinct memory-database directory never triggers it, matching the HLD's own L-01-aligned statement 'MUST NOT place memory tables in the existing index store or reuse its connection singleton.' No existing Story's ownership contract is touched. [files: src/db/lance/conn.ts, docs/epics/share-project-memory-across-agents-applications-E2026110117123b6d/HLD.md]

findings.premise: The HLD's own durable queue (sc3 DurableQueue/QueueFrame) is not a redesign of the daemon's existing in-memory IndexJob queue/lane mechanism; the two remain entirely separate ownership domains.
findings.evidence: src/daemon/queue.ts's two lanes operate over `IndexJob` objects for code-index/summary work and never persist to disk; the HLD's sc3 DurableQueue operates over `MemoryCommand`/`QueueFrame` objects with disk-backed segments, checksums and recovery semantics — disjoint types, disjoint storage, no shared ownership claimed by either artifact. [files: src/daemon/queue.ts, docs/epics/share-project-memory-across-agents-applications-E2026110117123b6d/HLD.md]

findings.premise: The HLD requires explicit versioning of public API/IPC/frame/schema/normalizer/embedding metadata plus a resumable migration/re-embedding command that preserves source identity and deletion guards, addressing compatibility for older records.
findings.evidence: HLD §'Forgetting, evidence and compatibility': 'Version public API, IPC, frame/schema, normalizer and embedding metadata... A migration/re-embedding command is resumable through the same writer and preserves source identity, deletion guards and reader freshness.' This matches requirements doc items L-05 and OD-09 (embedding migration and store maintenance, confirmed present at docs/reqs/shared-project-memory.html line 285 and 508). [files: docs/epics/share-project-memory-across-agents-applications-E2026110117123b6d/HLD.md, docs/reqs/shared-project-memory.html]

findings.premise: The HLD correctly treats the installed LanceDB version's atomicity/nullable-vector/read-consistency behavior as unqualified rather than assumed, consistent with the actually-pinned dependency version in this repo.
findings.evidence: package.json pins "@lancedb/lancedb": "0.40.0" exactly. The HLD states: 'If installed Lance cannot meet the documented atomicity, nullable-vector and read consistency contract, stop s3 for a reviewed design amendment rather than split authority across stores' — it does not assert the physical schema already works against 0.40.0, matching the fact that no such qualification exists yet in this codebase for a per-directory memory table. [files: package.json, docs/epics/share-project-memory-across-agents-applications-E2026110117123b6d/HLD.md]

findings.premise: The sc2 MemoryFailure error-code union covers the major failure classes the requirements doc's crash/failure and acceptance tables name (second-writer conflict, queue exhaustion, stale revision, store outage, context overflow, incompatible protocol version, policy/privacy denial).
findings.evidence: sc2's MemoryFailure.code = 'INVALID_REQUEST'|'UNBOUND_PROJECT'|'POLICY_DENIED'|'BACKPRESSURE'|'NOT_READY'|'UNSUPPORTED_VERSION'|'OWNERSHIP_CONFLICT'|'REVISION_CONFLICT'|'STORE_UNAVAILABLE'|'CONTEXT_OVERFLOW'|'DEADLINE_EXCEEDED' maps 1:1 onto requirements rows AC-21 (second writer→OWNERSHIP_CONFLICT), AC-16 (queue capacity→BACKPRESSURE), U-01 (stale correction→REVISION_CONFLICT), AC-28 (store outage→STORE_UNAVAILABLE), AC-24 (budget overflow→CONTEXT_OVERFLOW), AC-31 (version mismatch→UNSUPPORTED_VERSION) and AC-25 (privacy→POLICY_DENIED). [files: docs/epics/share-project-memory-across-agents-applications-E2026110117123b6d/HLD.md, docs/reqs/shared-project-memory.html]

findings.premise: A one-candidate-fails-in-a-batch scenario (AC-13 / recovery-table row 'One candidate in a batch fails') is detectably handled because the HLD commits one event's entire row set as a single atomic table mutation, so the retry unit is unambiguous.
findings.evidence: HLD §'Processing, consistency and mutable memory': 'Prepare one event's full row set and apply it with one qualified table mutation, including receipt and generation.' This satisfies the requirements doc's first allowed option at that row — 'Retry the atomic unit' — rather than leaving the choice (atomic-unit retry vs. per-candidate accounting) unresolved. [files: docs/epics/share-project-memory-across-agents-applications-E2026110117123b6d/HLD.md, docs/reqs/shared-project-memory.html]

findings.premise: The HLD establishes a traceability discipline requiring every owning Story LLD to trace its test cases back to the authoritative, cited AC-01 through AC-32 set in the requirements document.
findings.evidence: HLD §'Qualification and traceability': 'The authoritative requirements input is docs/reqs/shared-project-memory.html (all numbered requirements and AC-01 through AC-32)... Owning LLDs must trace their cases to these requirements.' Grep confirms AC-01 through AC-32 exist verbatim at docs/reqs/shared-project-memory.html lines 442–473 (32 distinct rows, each with a concrete required observation). [files: docs/epics/share-project-memory-across-agents-applications-E2026110117123b6d/HLD.md, docs/reqs/shared-project-memory.html]

findings.premise: The HLD itself allocates which of the 32 requirements-doc acceptance criteria (AC-01..AC-32) belong to which of its nine stories, so that each AC is traceable to exactly the story responsible for testing it.
findings.evidence: Grepping the HLD body for the pattern 'AC-\d+' returns exactly ONE occurrence — the single summary line naming the range 'AC-01 through AC-32' — with no per-story breakdown anywhere in §6 story boundaries or §8 rollout. The DEF's own per-story acceptance criteria use a disjoint, unrelated numbering (ac1/ac2/ac3 per story, operationalizing constraints k1–k6), confirmed by a zero-match grep for 'AC-\d+' in DEF.md. No document in this epic currently maps the 32 authoritative ACs onto S001–S009, so a story owner has no HLD-level record of which of the 32 criteria it must cover. [files: docs/epics/share-project-memory-across-agents-applications-E2026110117123b6d/HLD.md, docs/epics/share-project-memory-across-agents-applications-E2026110117123b6d/DEF.md, docs/reqs/shared-project-memory.html]
findings.action: Add an explicit AC-01..AC-32 → story (s1..s9) allocation table to the HLD (or to each Story's forthcoming LLD at minimum) before approving further LLDs, so no requirements-doc acceptance criterion is silently dropped between the DEF's ac1/ac2/ac3 labels and the reqs doc's AC-01..32 labels.
